knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The designated route keeps soiled and clean flow apart. The cleaner uses it and tells the supervisor if it is blocked, instead of taking a shortcut across a soiled area.
A used cloth on a clean shelf is a cross-contamination event. The cloth is removed, clean items it touched are set aside, and the supervisor is told. Cleaned items are not returned to stock.
Each zone has its own cloths and equipment, identified by the facility's colour or label system, so contamination does not carry from one zone to another.

practicalCriteria: Given a shortest route through a soiled holding area and a longer designated route, the learner takes the designated route and records it.
Given a used cloth found on the clean trolley shelf, the learner removes it, sets aside any clean items it touched, and tells the supervisor.
Given a bucket used in a bathroom and then carried into a resident room, the learner stops using it for that room, sets it aside, and reports which rooms were affected.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three checks means all three correct. Practical competence needs facility-observed assessment against the practical criteria, and a knowledge pass does not count as practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Route plan for the area showing the designated route
Cross-contamination event record with the time, the items and the person told
Observation note of zone equipment allocation
stopWorkCriteria: Learner carries used equipment onto a clean area or the clean trolley shelf
Learner returns a cross-contaminated item to clean stock
Learner uses a cloth from one zone in another zone
